Added echo feature and exit recognition
Mark as done completed with extension A-classes
Todo, events and deadlines added without extending Task class
Enhanced code to handle edge cases and possible errors
Tightened implementation against OS and relative file paths
Implemented java datetime handling for deadlines
Extract Ui class for console interaction
commitResults.messageBody:
Moves all direct System.out printing and Scanner reading out of Chud
into a new Ui class, as the first step of the OOP refactor extracting
Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList out of the main class. Chud's command
handling logic (the switch statement) is unchanged -- only the raw
println/print/Scanner calls were replaced with calls to ui.showX()/
ui.readCommand(), so console output is byte-for-byte identical
(verified via test-ui, 15/15 passing).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList class to wrap the task collection
commitResults.messageBody:
Second step of the Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList refactor. Introduces a
TaskList class wrapping the ArrayList<Task> behind named operations
(add/get/remove/size) and Iterable<Task>, so Chud and Storage work
through a task-list abstraction instead of a raw ArrayList. Storage.load()
still returns an ArrayList<Task> (as in the target design's sample
constructor, `tasks = new TaskList(storage.load())`); Storage.save() now
takes a TaskList.

Because TaskList's method names mirror ArrayList's, Chud's call sites
were untouched apart from the two lines that construct/type the list --
confirming the abstraction is a faithful wrapper, not a behavior change.
Verified via test-ui, 15/15 passing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser class to interpret user command text
commitResults.messageBody:
Third step of the Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList refactor. Moves all
"making sense of the raw command line" logic out of Chud's switch
statement into a new Parser class: splitting a line into command word
and arguments, parsing a task index, and parsing each command's
argument shape (a todo's description; a deadline's description and
/by date/time; an event's description and /from/to date/times; an
on query date). Every parsing failure still surfaces as the same
ChudException message as before.

Chud's switch cases now read as "parse via Parser, then execute
against tasks/storage/ui" -- the mutation, persistence, and printing
stay in Chud since that's the orchestration this refactor is building
towards, not something Parser should own. Command.fromCommandWord
dispatch was left where it is (on the Command enum itself), since
it's tightly co-located with the enum's own values.

Verified via test-ui, 15/15 passing -- no message text or console
output changed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Make Storage take its file path from the caller
commitResults.messageBody:
Fourth and final step of the Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList refactor.
Storage no longer hardcodes "data/chud.txt" internally; it now takes
the save file's path via its constructor, with Chud.main passing
"data/chud.txt" -- matching the target design's sample constructor
shape (`new Duke("data/tasks.txt")`).

The path is still resolved through Path.of (which accepts either '/'
or '\' as a separator), so it remains a relative, OS-independent
location; only where the literal path string lives changed, not how
it's parsed.

This also makes Storage reusable/testable against any file path
rather than a single fixed location, which is a natural side benefit
of dependency injection.

Verified via test-ui, 15/15 passing, plus a manual run from a machine
with no pre-existing data folder to confirm first-run creation still
works with the new constructor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename the Command word enum to CommandWord
commitResults.messageBody:
Prerequisite step for the Command-pattern stretch goal (AddCommand,
DeleteCommand, ExitCommand, etc. extending an abstract Command class).
The name Command is needed for that new class hierarchy, so the
existing enum -- which represents a recognized command word (LIST,
MARK, TODO, ...), not an executable action -- is renamed to
CommandWord to free it up. Pure rename, no behavior change.

Verified via test-ui, 15/15 passing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix CommandWord rename commit: apply the actual content changes
commitResults.messageBody:
The previous commit (04adeb5) renamed Command.java to CommandWord.java
via git-mv, but a race in how the changes were staged meant it
captured the file's old content -- CommandWord.java still declared
"public enum Command", which doesn't compile (a public class/enum's
name must match its file name). This commit applies the intended
content: enum Command -> CommandWord, fromCommandWord's local
variable/loop names updated to match, and Chud.java's one call site
(CommandWord.fromCommandWord(commandWord)) updated accordingly.

Verified via test-ui, 15/15 passing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageBody:
This project's code style has been ad hoc so far, applying no
single documented standard. Adopt the SE-EDU intermediate Java
coding standard (naming, layout, statements, comments/Javadoc)
as the project's convention.

Add the seedu-java-coding-standard skill as a checklist reference
for it, sourced from
https://se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/intermediate.html,
and mandate it in AGENTS.md for all Java code, new or edited, so
future changes are checked against it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The Git guidance in AGENTS.md was a brief, informal note ("include
enough detail to explain the rationale") rather than a documented
standard. Adopt the SE-EDU Git conventions (commit subject/body
format, branch naming) as the project's convention instead.

Add the seedu-git-standard skill as a checklist reference for it,

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The project now mandates the SE-EDU intermediate Java coding
standard for all code (see the new seedu-java-coding-standard
skill), but the existing codebase predates that rule and had a
few violations.

Fix import ordering across the files that had it backwards:
project packages (chud.*) must come after java.*/org.* imports,
not before. Wrap five lines that exceeded the style's 110-char
soft limit (a method signature, a long constant assignment, two
ternary expressions) using the standard's break-before-operator,
8-space-continuation rules. Add the missing Javadoc header
comments the standard requires on nearly every non-private class
and method -- Chud, Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, ChudException,
and all eight *Command constructors -- using @param/@return/
@throws where the standard calls for them.

Verified via ./gradlew test (83 JUnit tests) and the test-ui
console suite (16 cases): both still pass, since none of this
changes behavior, only formatting and documentation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Users had no way to locate a task without scrolling through the
full list. Add a find command that lists only the tasks whose
description contains a given keyword.

Add Task.matchesKeyword(String), a case-insensitive substring
check against the description only (not dates/times or type),
mirroring the existing occursOn(LocalDate) query-method pattern.
Add FindCommand plus CommandWord.FIND and a Parser.parseFindKeyword
helper, following the same Command/Parser split used by every other
command; an empty keyword is rejected the same way an empty todo
description is. Update the unknown-command message and the user
guide to mention find.

Verified via ./gradlew test (JUnit, including new Task and Parser
cases) and the test-ui console suite (17 cases, including a new one
covering matches, case-insensitivity, no matches, and the empty-
keyword error): both pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
